title: Climate carousel in Poland brings storms and strong winds
seoTitle: Climate carousel in Poland brings storms and strong winds
subtitle: The country records abrupt variations with the arrival of atmospheric fronts, fog and hail risk in the coming days.
excerpt: Poland faces a rapid weather shift as atmospheric fronts and low‑pressure systems Raphael and Tessa arrive in the next few days.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
Poland is experiencing rapid meteorological instability caused by the passage of atmospheric fronts from west to east, which has generated storm alerts and abrupt temperature changes. The phenomenon, locally described as a climate carousel, will bring rain, strong winds and even hail to several regions of the country in the coming days. This drastic shift in the atmosphere places Polish territory under the influence of different weather systems.

What the weather looks like on Polish Sunday

On Sunday, the scenario shows a quick transition. While the Saturday‑to‑Sunday night starts clear over most of the territory, the east records passing showers and dissipating storms, with precipitation of up to 10 liters of water per square metre and wind gusts up to 60 km/h. During Sunday daytime, the weather temporarily improves, bringing warmth and sunshine, with temperatures reaching 28 °C in the south of the country. However, cloudiness increases from the southwest, bringing isolated rain in the western half and local storms in Pomerania.

Fog and reduced visibility early in the day

Sunday morning requires extra caution from residents due to the formation of dense fog fronts. In the eastern and southern regions, visibility drops dramatically to about 300 metres during the early hours. This fog tends to dissipate throughout the morning, especially in the southern portion, giving way to cloud cover ranging from moderate to extensive, with temporary sun openings.

The arrival of the Raphael and Tessa systems on Monday

The meteorological situation becomes even more complicated on Monday, when Poland comes under the direct influence of two low‑pressure systems named Raphael and Tessa. These systems are secondary and derive from a large low‑pressure area covering all of Northern Europe, moving from the Atlantic Ocean eastward. The approach of these atmospheric fronts triggers a marked deterioration of the weather, with cloudiness increasing from moderate to total throughout the day.

Risks of strong storms and hail

With Raphael and Tessa active, Monday will see rain advancing from the west into the interior of the country. In Western Pomerania, the south, the centre and the east of Poland, local storms are forecast that can be quite severe. Meteorologists point to the risk of torrential rain accumulating 20‑30 liters of water per square metre, as well as the possibility of hail. During the thunderstorms, wind gusts may reach 70‑90 km/h, representing a sharp contrast with the weak to moderate winds of Sunday.

With information from wPolsce24, TVN24.
